title: P6a2: scorecard review quality — reviews by verdict, findings per review by severity, distinct defects across the two reviews of one task (overlap by path and line, and by normalised issue text), tokens and cost per review and findings per million tokens, grouped by reviewer role, packet version, reviewer tier and complexity band; CLI scorecard --reviews; baseline snapshots include it
spec:
Phase I P6 (brief inlined: measure whether reduced review context affects review findings; never remove reviews to save tokens). Base goal/T-0489 after P6a1 (T-0491) merges: attribution.review_facts(review_task) gives verdict, findings_count, findings_by_severity, reviewer_role, checklist_used, reviewed_sha, packet_version, review_pass_index, reviews_expected for every review task, old or new; review run rows carry the same keys plus tokens and usd. Work only in your own worktree and commit only on your own branch.
1. scorecard.review_quality(root=STATE, by="role") -> dict; by in ("role", "packet_version", "tier", "band", "reviewed_executor"). Rows: every review task joined to its run row(s) through _attributed and to the reviewed task (inputs[0]). Per group: n_reviews, verdicts {approve, request_changes, other}, findings_per_review (mean, median), findings_by_severity totals, share_of_reviews_with_a_high_finding, tokens_per_review (median), usd_per_review (median, None when unknown), findings_per_million_tokens, and for reviewed tasks with two done reviews: distinct_defects (union of comments deduplicated by (path, line) and by the first 60 normalised characters of issue), overlap_share (comments found by both reviews / union), second_review_added (findings only the pass-2 review had). packet_version None groups as "pre-packet" so history before P1b is comparable with rows after it. None for undefined values (H1 rule).
2. CLI: orchestrator scorecard --reviews [--by role|packet_version|tier|band|reviewed_executor] [--json]; the flag is exclusive with --efficiency, --economics and --routing (the same error message convention as backlog B1 T-0488: "choose one of --economics, --efficiency, --routing, --reviews"; if B1 is not yet merged into this branch, implement the check here for --reviews only and keep the others unchanged).
3. baseline.save includes review_quality(root) for by in ("role", "packet_version") under efficiency.reviews; baseline.compare reports findings_per_review, share_of_reviews_with_a_high_finding and distinct_defects as non-inferiority metrics (a drop is flagged worse) and tokens_per_review as a primary metric.
4. README: under the Efficiency telemetry section, ten lines on review quality and how to compare packet versions.
Tests tests/test_scorecard.py (synthetic review tasks with comments and run rows): test_review_quality_counts_verdicts_and_findings_by_severity, test_review_quality_distinct_defects_and_overlap_for_two_reviews, test_review_quality_groups_by_packet_version_with_pre_packet_bucket, test_review_quality_findings_per_million_tokens_and_none_when_no_tokens; tests/test_cli.py::test_cli_scorecard_reviews_text_and_json; tests/test_baseline.py::test_baseline_includes_review_quality_and_compare_flags_drops. Existing tests green; full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exit 0; commit with the task id including every named test; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: scorecard --reviews reports the metrics above by role, packet_version, tier, band and reviewed_executor with a pre-packet bucket; baseline compare flags drops in findings per review, high-finding share and distinct defects as worse
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree; the commit is on this task's own branch
